comparator.academicYear: Current prospective curriculum pages checked 2026-09-25 (concurrent year overviews)
comparator.route: Ordinary PPS programme with six student-selected thematic modules
comparator.sourceNotes: The three prospective year overviews sum to 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one has twelve 5-EC compulsory philosophy and skills courses. Year two has a 10-EC compulsory project and 5-EC Power of Words plus three student-chosen 15-EC PPS modules; year three has 5-EC Philosophy in Practice and 10-EC thesis plus three such modules. Each module comprises three 5-EC courses and themes are selected by students; one or two module substitutions from other faculty courses may be possible. The alternative semester-one/semester-two thesis listing is counted once. The zero-credit RADAr assessment is excluded. Prospectus pages describe concurrent years and do not guarantee one entrant-cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, politics and contemporary society
alternatives.concept: A broad UCR philosophy and politics route integrates philosophical history, ethics, selfhood, political theory, international institutions, rhetoric, society and critical examination of new technologies and environmental justice. Radboud teaches a sustained philosophy-first curriculum and six dedicated PPS thematic modules; UCR distributes this study across separate disciplines.
alternatives.labelReason: Broad philosophical and political content is visible in the scheduled courses, without implying the six Radboud modules are replicated.
progression: All 24 distinct courses have an X in their assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, required prerequisites appear earlier, and the plan has at least six 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Technology, ecological change and political ethics
alternatives.concept: This distinct path keeps philosophical foundations while studying AI ethics, environmental change, climate communication, media and public persuasion. It engages the digital and ecological PPS module interests across UCR disciplines without equating those courses to Radboud philosophical modules.
alternatives.labelReason: Digital and ecological courses provide a visible sustained thematic shift from the broad closest route.
progression: All 24 distinct courses have an X in their assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, required prerequisites appear earlier, and the plan has at least six 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This path changes 6 courses against alternative 1, with sustained coursework in its own stated theme.

alternatives.label: Global justice, human rights and democracy
alternatives.concept: This path concentrates political philosophy, comparative politics, human-rights law, international law, constitutional systems, European institutions, conflict and social movements. It answers a PPS interest in global justice and democratic futures but is more legal and empirical than Radboud’s philosophy-first modules.
alternatives.labelReason: A sustained rights and democratic institutions sequence distinguishes this path from the other two.
progression: All 24 distinct courses have an X in their assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, required prerequisites appear earlier, and the plan has at least six 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This path changes 4 courses against alternative 1, 8 courses against alternative 2, with sustained coursework in its own stated theme.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary PPS programme with six student-selected thematic modules
routeSelection.basis: No named theme is mandatory for all students. Six 15-EC module slots remain genuine constrained choice; the comparison does not assume a particular sequence of modules or turn the theme menu into requirements.

selection.assessment: Three feasible 24-course UCR programmes preserve a broad closest philosophy-and-politics response and two distinct technology/ecology and global-justice/democracy thematic responses. Mental-health and intercultural/gender interests are separately assessed but do not create a fourth pathway under the three-alternative cap.

notes.text: UCR combines philosophy, political theory, sociology, law, communication, media and environmental courses. Radboud has a philosophy-first 60-EC introductory year followed by six dedicated, student-selected philosophical modules and its own thesis. The UCR choices are related academic paths, not course equivalencies or credit-transfer advice.
